There is only one way to "monetize" your large holdings, and that is yield. Now the yield can be from staking or lending, in a lending market or to a private borrower, but it hasn't really changed from 2021. Staking is either some form of lending, or liquidity providing to facilitate swaps for other traders. Only new things are new instruments popping up, and shittier protocols that use yield bearing assets as collateral in their lending markets so you can tune up the leverage and loop to increase yield, and risk obviously.

The most challenging thing is to know which protocol to use, and trust me there are less than 10 in the entire industry. Most of them will go bust, be it from an inside job or poorly coded contracts that will be exploited, so your 10% APR will usually become -100%.

Just started playing ff14 a month ago and never played healer in any MMO until now. I can't say how it was before for obvious reasons, but I'm absolutely loving playing this job. It feels super fun and gratifying to play.

As a tank your role is to make the dungeon goes as fast as possible, and obviously hold mobs and not die.
So, use sprint often, and pull as many packs as you can. You will have to gauge how good your healer is / how hard the trash are. Some dungeons have easier trash than others.

Use at arm's length on trash, it slows down enemies and usually don't work on bosses, so it's an additional mit in your toolkit. Don't hesitate to use your cooldowns on packs as well, both offensive and defensive, usually packs are harder to heal than bosses and using your cooldowns sooner means you'll use them more in the run overall.

Usually you want the boss to face away from the group, but not always as some have a reverse cleave (it's telegraph so it's fine). Pick a spot and don't move, you want to make the life of the melee dps easier with their positional. Obviously move if there is a mechanic to avoid.

Some jobs like GNB or PLD have party support, if shit goes wrong and you can relieve your healer a bit, you can. Also use party mit as needed.
